name: University of Reading

settingEvidence.evidence: Our beautiful Whiteknights campus is the hub of University of Reading life.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (home) students starting in 2027 (2027/28). Reading says the home fee is subject to annual increases in later years of study.

source.evidence: The home tuition fee for 2027 entry is £10,050.

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £166-£365 a week in 2026/27, depending on room type: standard rooms £166.32-£234.85, upgraded £180.39-£244.23, premium £194.88, townhouse £213.57-£220.15, en suite £217.07-£295.33, flats £285.11-£364.70 (flats are often chosen by families and postgraduates but are also open to undergraduates).

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 7 November 2026 (the page does not print the year; 7 November is a Saturday in 2026). Later dates not announced yet.

source.evidence: Saturday 7 November

contextual.summary: Applicants who meet at least one of Reading's contextual criteria (for example a low-participation or deprived postcode, a declared disability, care experience, or taking part in Reading Scholars) get an offer typically two grades lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically two grades lower than the top end of the published grade range (for example ABB becomes BBC); one grade lower again if you are taking an EPQ.

criteria.detail: Live in an area with low participation in higher education (POLAR quintiles 1 and 2). You must be classed as a 'Home' student and have the correct Postal/Home postcode on your UCAS form. The page does not say which POLAR version.
Live in an area with high levels of deprivation (IMD quintiles 1 and 2). You must be classed as a 'Home' student and have the correct Postal/Home postcode on your UCAS form.
Have declared a disability on your UCAS form (choose the most appropriate option from the disability list).
Took part in Reading's Reading Scholars programme (contact outreach@reading.ac.uk for details).
Care experienced (select this category on your UCAS form).
Refugees or asylum seekers (select this category on your UCAS form).
Estranged from your family (select this category on your UCAS form).
Young carer: responsible for unpaid care for a family member, partner or friend who could not cope without your support; you must be 25 or under.

Child of a military family (service child): a parent or guardian currently serving in the UK Regular Armed Forces or as a reservist, or who has done so at any point in the first 25 years of your life; you must be 25 or under.

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers go to applicants who meet at least one of the listed criteria. The offer applies whether Reading is your firm or insurance choice, and you still need any subject-specific and GCSE requirements. If you are also taking an EPQ the contextual offer is lowered by one more grade (for example BBB becomes BBC). No contextual offers are made for programmes with a Foundation Year.

source.evidence: That is why we make contextual offers to applicants who meet at least one of the following criteria:

programmes.name: Reading Scholars
programmes.summary: Free Year 12 programme (on-campus days, a 4-day residential and online mentoring) giving a taste of university life; if you complete it and apply to Reading you are guaranteed an interview or a conditional offer, usually two grades lower.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students with at least five GCSEs at grade 4 or above including Maths, English and Science, on course for good A-level (or equivalent) grades. The programme is targeted at priority groups (for example living in a low progression postcode area, or care experienced). Some subject strands need specific A-levels.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Targeted at students in Reading's priority groups, for example living in a low progression postcode area or Looked After/Care Experienced. The full selection criteria are in a Word document linked from the page, which could not be read.
benefits: All costs covered in advance (transport, lunch, refreshments and accommodation for on-campus events)
Guaranteed invitation to interview or conditional offer if you apply to Reading
A two grade drop on your offer for most courses
You can apply for a £1,000 Reading Scholars bursary in your first year if Reading is your first choice
programmes.offerReduction: a two grade drop on their offer for most courses
programmes.subjects: Subject strands in 2026 included Business and Philosophy, Politics and Economics (no stand-alone Economics strand), plus Law, Psychology, History and others

courses.notes: Henley Business School course (Real Estate and Planning). Henley's undergraduate page says Henley is based at the University of Reading's Whiteknights campus (https://www.henley.ac.uk/study/undergraduate). Core modules include Introductory Economics for Business and Finance and Real Estate and Urban Economics. The first two years are shared with the other Real Estate and Planning degrees and course transfers are available after year 1 or 2. Deferred entry available. Reading's BSc Real Estate Finance and BSc Real Estate Development and Planning were not researched. Reading says all offers exclude General Studies, and that the entry requirements on course pages are only an indicator (https://www.reading.ac.uk/ready-to-study/study/how-to-apply/entry-requirements-ug). An integrated International Foundation Year is described for international/EU students only.

notes: All eight course pages show 2027/28 entry (the newest published; Reading's course finder lists only 2026/27 and 2027/28), so all courses use 2027 entry.

Reading is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry (https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/01172717/Course_List_2027_Entry_Final.pdf), and none of the course pages checked names an admissions test.
Real Estate is a Henley Business School course; Henley's undergraduate page says it is based at the University of Reading's Whiteknights campus (https://www.henley.ac.uk/study/undergraduate).

Subject taster days exist (past events included a PPE Taster Day on 2 July 2026 and a Real Estate Planning and Development taster on 10 June 2026) but the page gives no year group or cost and no 2027 dates, so they are not recorded as a programme (https://www.reading.ac.uk/ready-to-study/visiting-and-open-days/taster-sessions).

Not researched: other related Reading subject areas listed on its site (Accounting; Business and Management, Accounting and Finance; Finance), BSc Real Estate Finance and BSc Real Estate Development and Planning.
